industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): technology saw $5.5 billion of net selling in the week, the most since January 2025 (Jefferies, 17 Oct), the rotation came out of it, and Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made'; against that, Jefferies finds sector pockets still upgrading inside it (analogue chips, optical networking, artificial-intelligence memory) and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, B prior at industry level, carried by Semiconductors at A. The industry row stays C because the industry is split: Semiconductors (D), Software B2B Enterprise (D), Fintech (D) and Games (D) carry the Underweight; IT services, Hardware and vertical software stay Neutral. Counter-case for D: the heaviest net selling in 21 months is a regime statement; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged, with the sector now split by the sources. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): artificial-intelligence-linked semiconductors fell eight straight sessions to 16 Oct, technology net selling was the heaviest since January 2025, Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made', Korea fell about 20% in October on de-grossing, and the AI credits that set this row (the neoclouds) are 'the epicentre of the funding cost debate' (Goldman, 19 Oct); against it, Jefferies (22 Oct) is 'incrementally positive' on analogue chips with a read-across to Infineon and STMicroelectronics, sees China's equipment imports up 26% as the upside for 2027-28, and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive, while on equipment Jefferies' own headline is 'ASML - Still not excited'. Neither condition for C is met (no stabilisation read on the AI credits; no sell-side buy call on the European sector). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior, the disagreement stated: the market still ranks the sector first while cutting its multiple. Ten of the 149 Pool stocks. Counter-case: the analogue upcycle 'has more legs' into 2027, demand was never the problem, and a D on ten Pool names pushes the Lists away from the one European industry with upgrades; the analogue read is a reason to look at STMicroelectronics stock by stock, not to move a row that is mostly equipment.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park, with an entry level. ASML (ASML-NL) at 1,507.4 EUR (2026-09-22) is a 'Demand Inflection' case in a monopoly, read late: the change is real, sector-wide, customer-funded and has travelled all six layers of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain, but the price already carries the two years of growth the record can see. On our modal path the 'Modal return' is 2.9 percent a year over eighteen months and 6.0 percent a year over three years, an F against the 20 percent bar; the plausibly worse drop-through takes the eighteen-month return to minus 3.3 percent. The park rule does not park it (management A, business quality A, predictability A, trackability B); the return parks it. The case becomes bullish and progressable at about 1,200 EUR on the eighteen-month test (about 1,250 EUR at the ten-year median multiple; about 1,110 EUR under the adverse drop-through), or at the current price if the January 2027 results confirm the 2028 low-NA EUV capacity of about 110 systems ordered and the 10 June 2027 Capital Markets Day raises the 2030 framework to a midpoint above 70 billion EUR. Conviction medium: a Triaging-stage working hypothesis whose two decisive facts are dated and observable. What to own is settled by the business, the structure and the fit; at what price is settled by the return and the multiple; at 1,507.4 EUR the second answer overrides the first.
case: The change is external, sector-wide and paid for by customers' cash. AI infrastructure demand lifts lithography intensity at logic and memory simultaneously: EUV layers rise from three at 1b DRAM to eight at 1d, 1c needs five to six, DRAM EUV exposures are forecast up 4.5 times over five years, HBM consumes three to four times the wafer capacity of standard DRAM. TSMC raised 2026 capex to USD 60 to 64 billion from USD 52 to 56 billion; N2 entered volume production ahead of schedule; SK hynix holds long-term agreements with about ten customers carrying deposits; WFE is about USD 145 billion in 2026, forecast USD 193 billion in 2027 and USD 220 billion in 2028. Management says it is close to receiving all orders for 2027 low-NA capacity of about 85 systems; 2028 bookings are substantial; the down payments are non-refundable. The edge of visibility is 2028: not all 85 tools for 2027 have firm final orders (Jefferies) and the 110 for 2028 is under investigation, not committed.

The company's response is a change force of its own. Guidance raised twice in six months; a 30 percent capacity build for 2027 with a further 30 percent under investigation, financed by customers; value-based pricing of 5 to 8 percent a year with zero discounting, framed around productivity on new models (NXE:3800F and 3800G); the E-to-F transition gives 45 percent more wafer capacity on 30 percent more units; a 1,700-position delayering estimated to save about 200 million EUR a year (ING), deferred to May 2027 by a union compromise; a 12 billion EUR buyback for 2026 to 2028; Brainport campus construction from Q3 2026, operational end-2028; the Zeiss framework restated with interest-free loans (610.0 million EUR drawn at end-2025). The screen's red flags are absent: a four-year chief-executive mandate to April 2028, capacity being built not presented, two raises, no crown jewels sold, the Mistral AI stake about 0.5 percent of market value, net cash, a cash-funded buyback. Internal forces rate B, not A, because they are a response to external demand rather than a transformation of a weak business, and the pattern to watch is capacity built at the top of the cycle.

The outputs have already done what the pattern asks. Q2 2026 revenue plus 21.3 percent, gross margin 54.0 percent driven by more than 1 billion EUR of software productivity upgrades at 100 percent gross margin, EBIT margin 37.1 percent, EPS plus 29 percent; four consecutive quarterly revenue beats of 2.3 to 2.9 percent over the guided midpoint; gross margin above the top of guidance in three of the last five quarters. Key metrics rate A on the framework's conditional rule: revenue growth from plus 2.6 percent (FY2024) and plus 15.6 percent (FY2025) to plus 35 percent guided for FY2026 and plus 27.1 percent consensus FY2027; operating margin from 34.6 percent to about 41 percent on our FY2026 path (consensus 40.5 percent), about 43 percent FY2027, 44.5 percent FY2028. Cash conversion is the weak metric (88.8 percent FY2025 but 12.0 percent FY2023; Q4 2025 free cash flow 10,940 EURm on down payments, Q1 2026 minus 2,608 EURm; net working capital 19,484 EURm, 55.2 percent of trailing revenue; 6.2 billion EUR of receivables factored). The sell-side has re-based (FY2027 consensus EPS up 74.7 percent, FY2028 up 98.6 percent in twelve months) and the wave has crested (one-month moves plus 0.1 to plus 1.3 percent). Sell-side upgrades over the next six to twelve months rate C: FY2026 is fixed by guidance (consensus 44,034 EURm at the midpoint), our FY2027 51.5 EUR is below the 54.10 EUR median and our FY2028 62 EUR below 70.31 EUR; not D because the top half of the FY2026 range is unclaimed (Huatai expects a record 14.4 billion EUR Q4), the 2028 decision is a live upgrade trigger and the skew is positive.
counter_case: In its strongest form: lithography intensity is rising structurally, not cyclically, and we have mistaken a structural re-basing for a cyclical peak. Each DRAM node adds EUV layers (three at 1b, five to six at 1c, eight at 1d); each logic node adds exposures; High-NA insertion at memory around 2028 and at Intel now opens a second product cycle; value-based pricing lifts ASP about 5 percent a year without list-price increases; Installed Base Management grows about 11 percent a year with a fleet that never shrinks; customers are funding the capacity with 18.9 billion EUR of non-refundable down payments; the supply constraint at Zeiss means the cycle cannot overshoot into gluts as deposition and etch did; sovereign money underwrites the fabs. On that reading FY2029 EPS of 90 EUR-plus is not extrapolation but arithmetic on capacity already being built; the company's 2030 framework is simply two years stale and will be raised in June 2027; and the right multiple for a monopoly compounding at 20 percent is the five-year median of 25x or the equipment peers' 33 to 34x, not the ten-year median. At 25x on 95 EUR of twenty-four-month-forward earnings the shares are worth about 2,400 EUR in eighteen months, an A return, and the sell-side's median target of 2,100 EUR (2026-09-18) is conservative. At 1,507.4 EUR the shares stand on about 16.5x consensus FY2029 EPS of 91.64 EUR, a multiple with no precedent in the stock's own history for a monopoly growing 30 percent. The 2028 capacity of about 110 systems will be ordered by mid-2027 as 2027's 85 were: "investigating" has meant "ordered" once already, and the order book filled before the tools were built. The houses making this argument (Bernstein: 2029 EPS 22 percent above consensus on a 60 percent gross margin, the market underestimates product-led pricing; Morgan Stanley: the margin story arrived a year early, a bull case of 2,600 EUR; Deutsche Bank: a clear line of sight to a gross margin above 60 percent) have had the better record on this stock for two years. Our FY2029 plateau is a base-rate judgement, not a datum; nothing in the research shows demand falling in 2029. If they are right the return is an A and our entry level is never reached.

At the 'Change Forces' level the competing reading is the Risks research's "false friend": the near-term force is a stockpiling and scarcity artefact, China pre-buying ahead of export bans inflated DUV to 2025, cleanroom scarcity inflates software upgrades now (Jefferies sizes the margin at 200 basis points), and the 2027 to 2028 capacity lands as AI capital spending is questioned. At the 'Foundations' level: a customer-financed monopoly whose robustness is borrowed (12.0 percent cash conversion in FY2023; four customers 61 percent of revenue; one German supplier can stop the company; one act of Congress can remove 15 percent of sales) is not robust, whatever its margins. At the 'Investment Setup' level: this is a 'Compounder' mis-modelled on pricing and margin, so consensus is structurally too low.
triggers: - The 2028 low-NA EUV capacity decision (about 110 systems) at the January 2027 results, with the annual backlog and FY2027 guidance: ordered is the single datum that moves our FY2029 from 68 EUR toward 85 EUR and the 'Investment Thesis' from C to B; not decided is the Alarm; not ordered by mid-2027 is the Invalidate level for the Key Driver.

- The 10 June 2027 Capital Markets Day: a 2030 frame with a midpoint above 70 billion EUR and 2028 orders in hand invalidates our plateau and makes the case progressable at the current price; a midpoint at or below 70 billion EUR is the Alarm on the 2029 Key Risk.

- Price: about 1,200 EUR clears the bar on our modal path (about 1,250 EUR at 23.5x; about 1,110 EUR under the adverse drop-through); a break below the 200-day average (1,313.61 EUR) is the Alarm on the de-rating Key Risk and the point at which the cyclical red-flag pattern would form.

- China: Q4 2026 China system sales below 2.5 billion EUR is the Alarm on the China Key Driver and on the top-line red flag; committee progress on the MATCH Act is the Alarm on the ban; enactment is the Invalidate level.

- Gross margin: Installed Base Management revenue down more than 20 percent sequentially in Q1 2027 (or below 2.8 billion EUR sequentially) confirms the bear reading; rising through the 2027 ramp confirms the bull; a quarter below the 54 percent guidance floor with no one-off named is the Invalidate level.
- Customer capital: a TSMC capex guidance cut of more than 10 percent (October 2026 or January 2027) is the Alarm on AI capital spending, customer concentration and the units Key Driver.
